text:
emily: thinking about the sequencer ordering for onboarding checks — we currently run fast-smoke -> bench -> deep-compat in series. that means slow models block the whole intake. can we discuss a fallthrough model?

sam: yep. proposal: run fast-smoke sync, then async fanout to bench + deep-compat. sequencer would mark as "pending-deep" and let runtime accept a lightweight "quarantine" tag so Dedicated can still serve a pinned version.

jess: hmm i worry about correctness/latency for customer-facing routes if we let questionable models through with "quarantine". what would the traffic split look like?

emily: split idea: 0% prod for quarantine, but allow internal/test routes + shadow traffic. only promote after bench+compat pass or manual signoff. avoids blocking intake queue.

tony: agree on queue pressure. also we should add a fail-slow path: if bench fails but deep-compat passes, sequencer triggers a rerun with relaxed sampling and flags for manual review. avoids spurious rejects on flaky perf.

sam: alternatives considered: (a) strict gate (current) — simpler but high latency; (b) probabilistic acceptance — lets some % through to detect runtime regressions earlier; (c) quarantine/fanout — like emily suggested. i prefer (c).

jess: +1 to (c) but we need clear semantics in the API: consumers must be able to opt-in to "quarantine models" and metrics must reflect that. otherwise people will think model is prod-ready.

qa-ops: can we add an automated stability checklist that runs when sequencer sees bench variance > 10%? small list: cold-start latency, kv-cache miss-rate, max-alloc. that microcheck can block promotion.

emily: good call. propose adding a micro-scan step (30s) after bench completes that samples 50 traces across seqlen buckets. if any bucket trips threshold, mark as "needs-warmup" and schedule a warmed-bench in the background.

sam: config sketch:
```yaml
sequencer:
  fast_smoke: sync
  bench: async
  deep_compat: async
  fallthrough_policy: quarantine
  micro_scan_samples: 50
  promote_on: bench_pass & compat_pass & micro_scan_pass
```

tony: two more tradeoffs: telemetry cost (we're duplicating runs) and determinism of rollbacks. need an idempotent promotion flow with audit logs so we can revert. also ensure rollouts are deterministic: `rollout: canary-5->20->100`

jess: +emoji :+1: on audit logs. small UX ask: console should show sequencer state machine (fast_smoke -> pending_deep -> quarantine -> promoted) with timestamps and links to bench artifacts.

infra-bot: note: queued bench jobs for model m-35 queued on pool gpu-pool-2 (est wait 5m).

emily: next steps: draft RFC that formalizes quarantine semantics, micro-scan thresholds, and promotion conditions. assign owners for artifacts and console view. i'll take the RFC writeup, sam can draft the sequencer config shape, jess will spec UI surface.

sam: i'll add a small integration test that simulates bench fails + deep-compat pass to verify rerun + manual flagging flow.

jess: can we also add a metric baseline so we don't spam alerts for new models? maybe a rolling baseline per model family.

emily: yes — baseline per family, fallback to global baseline if family unknown. ok i'll start RFC now. thanks all. :sparkles:
